question: What does Radd-ul-Fasaad mean?
why: Radd means rejection and fasaad means disorder or strife, so the phrase means rejecting discord.
rel: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017. It was a nationwide counter-terrorism operation.

question: What is the currency of New Zealand?
why: New Zealand uses the New Zealand dollar (NZD), written NZ$.
rel: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand. Auckland is its largest city.

question: What is Pakistan’s longest river?
why: The Indus is Pakistan's longest river and the backbone of its irrigation.
rel: Major tributaries include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Sutlej and Kabul.

question: What is condensation?
options: Change of water vapour into liquid
why: Condensation is when water vapour cools and turns into liquid water.
rel: Clouds form by condensation. Evaporation is the opposite process.

question: Which languages/technologies are used to build websites?
why: HTML structures content, CSS styles it and JavaScript adds interactivity.
rel: Java and JavaScript are different languages. PHP is commonly used on the server side.

question: What does NATO stand for, and when was it established?
why: NATO means North Atlantic Treaty Organization and the treaty was signed on 4 April 1949.
rel: It was signed in Washington, D.C. with 12 founding members.

question: What percentage of Pakistan is covered by forests?
why: As of Oct 2026, the Pakistan Economic Survey (2026) puts forest area at about 4.1 million hectares, around 4.7% of land.
rel: Pakistan loses about 11,000 hectares of forest a year. Older and FAO figures such as 2.2% are also quoted.
problem: No single figure: 2.2% (FAO, often in old MCQ keys), 4.7% (Economic Survey 2026), 5.1% (PFI) all appear. Check the exam's key.

question: Complete: “He will ___ here by now.”
why: The future perfect uses will have plus past participle, so the answer is 'have reached'.
rel: Future perfect: will have + past participle. 'Arrive' is often preferred over 'reach here' in formal usage.

question: Which area is called Babul Islam?
why: Sindh is called Babul Islam, the Gateway of Islam, because Islam first entered the subcontinent here.
rel: Muhammad bin Qasim's campaign in Sindh took place in 711-712 CE.

question: How many major rivers are commonly listed for Balochistan?
why: Some general knowledge sources list seven major rivers for Balochistan.
rel: Rivers include Hingol, Dasht, Porali, Hub, Zhob, Nari and Bolan. Many are seasonal.
problem: Count depends on classification; 7 is the commonly quoted figure.

question: What is the inverse of a scalar matrix?
why: If A = aI with a not zero, then A inverse = (1/a)I, which is again scalar.
rel: A zero scalar matrix has no inverse because its determinant is zero.

question: What is the last letter when “UTYEAB” is arranged alphabetically?
why: Sorted alphabetically the letters are A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last is Y.
rel: Alphabetical order puts Y after U and T.

question: Which is Pakistan's largest district by area?
why: Chagai in Balochistan, about 44,748 sq km, is the largest district of Pakistan by area.
rel: As of Oct 2026 Chagai is still listed as the largest. Its headquarters is Dalbandin.

question: What is an empty set?
options: A set with exactly one element
A set containing only the number zero
why: The empty set has no elements, so its cardinality is zero.
rel: It is written as the symbol ∅ or { }. It is a subset of every set.

question: Who is known by the title “Kaleemullah”?
why: Kaleemullah means one who spoke with Allah, a title of Prophet Musa.
rel: Khalilullah is Prophet Ibrahim and Ruhullah is Prophet Isa.

question: Who was President when Pakistan's 1956 Constitution came into force?
why: Iskander Mirza became the first President when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
rel: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956. The constitution was abrogated in 1958.

question: Who partitioned Bengal in 1905?
why: Lord Curzon, the Viceroy, partitioned Bengal in 1905.
rel: The partition was annulled in 1911. It stimulated the Swadeshi Movement.

question: When did Abu Bakr (RA) lead the Hajj, and when was Hajj made obligatory?
why: Abu Bakr (RA) led the Hajj in 9 AH.

question: When was the Badshahi Mosque built?
why: The Badshahi Mosque, commissioned by Aurangzeb, was completed in 1673.
rel: It stands in Lahore opposite Lahore Fort. It was once among the world's largest mosques.

question: Which country voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in 1947?
why: Afghanistan cast the only vote against Pakistan's admission to the UN.

question: What was the approximate Muslim force at the Battle of Badr?
why: Traditional accounts say about 313 Muslims fought at Badr.

why: Zakat is commonly dated as made obligatory in 2 AH.

question: When is friction between a tyre and the road at its maximum useful level?
options: When the wheels are fully locked and sliding
When the tyre is stationary and unloaded
When the road is wet with zero tyre pressure
Just before the tyre starts to skid
why: Friction is highest near the limit of static friction, just before sliding begins.
rel: Locked sliding tyres have less friction than rolling tyres near peak grip. ABS prevents wheel lockup.
problem: Question is vague; many MCQ keys say 'hard braking'. Answer chosen is the scientific one.

question: Which Microsoft Word feature creates decorative text?
why: WordArt applies stylized, decorative effects to text.

question: Which battle is called Jang-e-Furqan?
why: Badr is called Jang-e-Furqan because it distinguished truth from falsehood.

question: Who enslaved Hazrat Bilal (RA) before his freedom?
why: Bilal (RA) was enslaved by Umayyah ibn Khalaf and tortured for accepting Islam.

question: What is the McMahon Line?
options: Eastern China-India boundary line (1914 Simla Convention)
why: The McMahon Line is the eastern sector boundary between China and India drawn at the 1914 Simla Convention.
rel: It is named after Henry McMahon. India accepts it but China disputes it.

question: What is the world's largest island?
why: Greenland is the world's largest island; Australia counts as a continent.

question: In which year did Shah Waliullah die?
why: Shah Waliullah died in 1762.
